brief: Democrats won both chambers in the midterms. The S&P 500 reversed an initial negative futures reaction to close 1.6% higher, Nasdaq gained 1.4%, the 10-year yield fell 8bps and the dollar index fell 0.5%. UBS says divided control plus Trump's veto power should make tax and spending changes harder to pass, removing an uncertainty source, though debt ceiling fights and Democratic gains in data center states, which could delay projects, raise costs or shift siting, are new risks. Hopes for US-Iran de-escalation via Qatari mediation, though Iran still wants its seven points met, sent Brent down 8.2% before it stabilized near 95 dollars. Depleted inventories, near complete SPR releases and tight freight and tanker capacity could still support oil, and renewed strikes remain a risk. Data center linked stocks fell on regulatory scrutiny fears while cash funded tech held up. UBS recommends rebalancing concentrated AI exposure toward quality, against a 1.0 to 1.5 trillion dollar capex forecast for 2026 to 2028 and a Chinese chip order surge UBS says confirms underlying demand. Separately, firmer Eurozone inflation feeds December ECB hike odds as US yields fell. UBS expects EURUSD to recover to 1.16 by year end.
